title: A Ledger for the Atlas
premise: In 1898, Ansel Iversen, a diver's daughter indentured to the Halvard Trading Company, keeps the workshop's ledger — the only record of every diver, debtor, and dead man in the coastal town of Skarnvik. When the army requisitions the town to erase its debts and conscript its people, the ledger becomes both evidence and death warrant. Ansel must copy and smuggle out the true names before the company burns the original, aided by the unlikely family she's gathered: a disgraced clerk, a deaf net-mender who reads lips, and the ghost of her drowned father's promises. She finishes the copy as the workshop burns around her, trading her own freedom for the truth's survival — and years later, from a prison cell, watches the ledger bring the company down.
about_author: Gideon Villalobos is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers from collapsed trading companies. They write historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Ansel Iversen, indentured since her father drowned in debt to the Halvard Company, works the workshop ledger by lamplight. POV: Ansel. She records a diver's death with cold efficiency until his widow spits at her feet. Emotional beat: the first crack in Ansel's belief that she merely writes history rather than makes it.

chapters.title: Gunboats at Dawn
chapters.summary: Army steamers anchor off Skarnvik; officers requisition the harbor, the warehouses, and the company's papers. POV: Ansel, watching from the drying racks. The company master orders the ledgers sealed for 'audit.' Emotional beat: dread hardening into defiance as Ansel realizes the names are the only thing standing between the townsfolk and erasure.

chapters.title: What the Net-Mender Saw
chapters.summary: Ansel confides in Maren, the deaf net-mender who reads lips across the whole town and knows which officers plan to burn the archives. POV: Maren, an outsider's clear-eyed view of Ansel. Emotional beat: the fragile beginning of found family — two women bound by what they've witnessed and nobody believes.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Kept Copies
chapters.summary: Disgraced ex-clerk Tobias Brandt, fired for falsifying entries he was ordered to falsify badly, reveals a hidden second ledger and offers to teach Ansel the company's cipher. POV: Tobias. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into purpose; the trio becomes a conspiracy of three.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers quarter in the workshop; Ansel serves them tea while memorizing which pages have already been removed. Her indenture contract is 'transferred' to army labor. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension — the enemy sleeping ten feet from the truth, and Ansel smiling through it.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Salt
chapters.summary: Maren's brother is conscripted using a forged debt entry Ansel herself recorded years ago. Grief and guilt fracture the group; Tobias argues for escape, Ansel for finishing the copy. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth — can Ansel be forgiven for being the pen?

chapters.title: The Cipher Night
chapters.summary: Working by stolen candle stubs, Ansel and Tobias decode the second ledger while Maren stands watch, signing warnings through the window. They discover the company sold divers' debts to the army itself. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: terrible clarity — the paper trail leads upward, and burning it protects the guilty.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Counting Room
chapters.summary: The company master discovers the missing pages and suspects Ansel; Tobias is arrested as the decoy and doesn't give her up. POV: Tobias, in a locked room choosing silence. Emotional beat: sacrifice as love — the found family holds even under interrogation.

chapters.title: Fire Is Also a Record
chapters.summary: Climax. Ordered to burn the archive herself, Ansel instead finishes the final copy as soldiers torch the workshop, smuggling the true ledger out inside Maren's nets. She lets herself be caught so the bundle escapes. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: triumph and loss braided together — the work survives because she does not go free.

chapters.title: Read Aloud in Another Country
chapters.summary: Years later, from a prison workhouse, Ansel receives word: the smuggled ledger has reached journalists and courts; the company collapses, Tobias freed, Maren's brother returned. A young clerk visits to take her testimony. POV: Ansel, older and unbroken. Emotional beat: quiet vindication — justice arrived late, outside the law, carried by ordinary hands.
